cells.tense: You are keeping the practice up right now, and it is holding steady.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Take what the practice has lately made plain and make a first thing from it — by hand, small enough to finish, and pointable-to when it's done. Begin at the plain part; stop at finished.
cells.core:
Steady practice and straight thinking, kept up over time — that's where you do well, and this is the good version of it. You've stayed with the work long enough that your judgment carries weight, and when someone comes to you lost, you can walk them through the part they can't see yet. Quiet work, mostly on your own, and it is earning its keep.

What this balance is free to feed next: making. Not more rehearsal stacked on rehearsal — the first compact thing that years of practice make possible, with edges you can point to when it's done. Keep it finishable, and finish it. That is how what you've held close becomes a thing in the world, and how the next question arrives.
cells.sheetLine: You know the work. Now it can be made.
cells.verb: directing a mind toward clarity through sustained practice
cells.place: where focused practice and refinement are kept up

cells.tense: You are rehearsing for a future that keeps not arriving, forcing a shape the work has not formed yet.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Let something go wrong in the practice and stay in it anyway. Keep the reason you started; set the tight grip aside and find out, from inside the friction, what still holds you.
cells.core:
When this goes past steady, practice stops being practice and turns into forcing. You're polishing for a moment that has not arrived, and the repetition that used to settle you now makes worry. Refining feels like preparing, but nothing meets the preparation, and the hours go into the gap.

Let the practice rub against something that resists, and do not smooth it. Technique does what it can; if the aim is alive, it survives without this particular grip. Stay in the difficult repetition long enough to feel what you're actually committed to. Whatever remains after that is the practice — lighter, and yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing for a future that won't hold still.
cells.verb: directing a mind toward clarity through sustained practice

cells.tense: The practice you were keeping up is behind you, and you are still standing at its door.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Do one right thing where nobody is watching and nobody is told. It can be quick. Let it be settled, not decided — you'll recognize it by how little it needs arguing.
cells.core:
Something that used to happen — sitting down with the work, keeping it up — stopped, and where it was there is now a quiet gap. Effort isn't what you're short of; the practical streak is still in you. What's gone silent is the inner sense of what's worth doing, which is why nothing has drawn you back.

Don't push at the practice directly. Start smaller: one case where the right move is already plain, done with no witness. That kind of act runs on what's settled in you and asks for no energy you don't have. Practice tends to come back the way it left — quietly, by way of what is yours to do.
cells.sheetLine: The practice stopped, and nothing has told you what's worth doing.
cells.verb: directing a mind toward clarity through sustained practice
cells.place: where focused practice and refinement are kept up

cells.tense: You are steering the practice from a room you are not standing in.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Let one person watch you do the practice, then do a piece of it beside you. Not a lesson — the work itself, shared, until it runs as one thing for a while.
cells.core:
You keep a discipline with real hours in it. The standard you hold was built by no one's instruction — you chose what to refine and kept at it — yet your telling of it makes it sound like something you happened to pick up. Decide it differently, and the account of how steady you are goes on skipping the part where you made it.

The way through is to stop doing the work alone for once. Not explaining it — doing it where one person can see, until their effort joins yours and the two run as one for an afternoon. Set beside you, it stops being only yours to know. Their account will say it before yours does.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is yours. Your telling of it isn't yet.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person's discipline is solitary cultivation 'kept lit by attention,' which the record does assume from the seat but which the reader could fairly say is different — their practice may happen in a group, a studio, a team. The asks survive being wrong: each is one small act that teaches the person something about where their steadiness is, whether or not my framing of the seat lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is the balanced core's turn about the person who can't yet see the way — that is the signature's own picture talking, so it comes out, or it stays my framing and not their life.
